"Unidentified male speaker: And who are you? "Momo Garic: Momo. "Unidentified male speaker: Momo who? "Momo Garic: Garic. "Unidentified male speaker: Tell me, Eric. "Momo Garic: Wait, wait, wait a second. Garic, this is Garic. "Unidentified male speaker: Oh Garic, go ahead. "Momo Garic: Is Veselinovic there? "Unidentified male speaker: No, Veselinovic is not there. "Momo Garic: Can you just can you help us, please? "Unidentified male speaker: Tell me, speak up! "Momo Garic: The army refuses, those tanks, we are encircled. Do you have any armours and manpower, please, I'm begging you. "Unidentified male speaker: Garic, Prstojevic is here. "Momo Garic: Let me talk to him. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Hello? "Momo Garic: Prstojevic? "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Yes. "Momo Garic: This is Garic. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Good morning. "Momo Garic: What's up? Listen. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Nothing special. "Momo Garic: How can you help us as soon as possible. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Help who? "Momo Garic: Us. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Who, where is that? "Momo Garic: Novo Sarajevo. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Yes, but where? What is your location? "Momo Garic: Just a second, we are at Vraca. We need some men in Vraca urgently, please. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Wait a second. Where are you in Vraca exactly? Are you down near the MUP or up there? "Momo Garic: Somebody will wait for those men at the pass. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Are you at the pass and further up on the right side? "Momo Garic: I will wait for the men at the pass. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Wait a second, Garic. Are you at the pass and further up on the right side towards Vraca. "Momo Garic: We went down to the town, all the way up to the Miljacka, but the army refuses to move and we are encircled. " Nedjelko Prstojevic: Wait a second, are you fighting there? "Momo Garic: We are fighting fiercely. We have many casualties. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Tonight, is that right? "Momo Garic: Well, no it started this morning here ... forget about it now. We are encircled as it seems. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Hmm. "Momo Garic: How can you help us? I also called Velibor in Nedzarici and he will try to do something, but that is not enough. That's not enough. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: All right. What are the special forces doing? "Momo Garic: They refuse to leave the barracks area. The special forces refuse to leave the barracks area. That's it. The reserve police force also promised to do everything they can but they went back. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Aha. "Momo Garic: That's it. "What are we going to do? "Nedjelko Prstojevic: You know, it's day-time and it is the south it is difficult to fight during the day in the south. "Momo Garic: Yes. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: And if they encircle you we cannot allow that. First of all we must not allow the encirclement and second ... "Momo Garic: Yes. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Yes. One can strike very well during the day. "So you have to organise yourself and get help from the people from the nearest surroundings. "Momo Garic: There is nobody closer than you. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: You have Vraca, Petrovici, and that area. "Momo Garic: There is nobody here. They've all gone down. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: They've all gone down? "Momo Garic: Yes. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Well if everybody's gone down, those must be very strong forces. "Momo Garic: Well them. We are stretched thin on, on all sides. Zlatiste. "So that's the problem. That is the problem. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Withdraw. I don't know, at this hour things here are going ... "Momo Garic: What? "Nedjelko Prstojevic: I don't know if I can give you any specific help right now. "At this moment. "Momo Garic: All right. All right. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Where are you fighting exactly? Where exactly are you ... "Momo Garic: Vrbanja, Grbavica, Ivan Krndelj to Elektroprivreda. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: And you went down, is that right? "Momo Garic: Yes, yes, yes. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Hem. "Well, if nothing else withdraw a little bit, with resilience, I mean. "Momo Garic: Yes. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Withdraw and mobilise all those people. "Momo Garic: Everybody's mobilised. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: Don't forget that it is difficult to send men to fight in an unknown area. "Momo Garic: Yes. All right. "Nedjelko Prstojevic: All right then. "Momir Garic: All right, goodbye!" "All right then, good-bye."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Garic, I'm sure you heard that in this conversation the person making the call identifies himself as Momo Garic. He says he's calling from Novo Sarajevo, specifically from Vraca. He says: "We are encircled." He says the army and the police refuse to assist and just as in the previous conversation we listened to he asks for manpower to be sent urgently from Ilidza to Vraca. Now, I know you said you didn't think you'd had any contacts with Mr. Prstojevic at the time, but this is clearly you speaking, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I do not remember those conversations, absolutely. It seems like a different world. I don't remember this conversation. I do not remember that I personally conducted that conversation. I repeat that I knew Prstojevic by sight. We didn't socialise. We did not communicate. And the truth is that the army really did not wish to extend any assistance to the unarmed people, very few people in this part of Sarajevo. And that's the truth. But however, I repeat the claim that I do not remember ever having conducted this conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Garic. Although you don't remember such conversation, do you confirm that it was your voice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. It's like a child's voice. It does not resemble my voice at all, absolutely not. It doesn't resemble my voice at all. This is my frank and personal opinion. This does not resemble my voice. I do not remember that I ever conducted this conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you agree, do you not, that the situation that this Momo Garic from Novo Sarajevo is describing is in your area; right? You were operating around Vraca and, in fact, as we mentioned earlier, you confirmed that Vraca -- there was a location in Vraca where your TO was located. So this was an operation of your TO forces, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Yes, the locality is at Vraca. This is where those things happened and this describes how it evolved, but we don't know anything about the operations that were going on, save for the fact that we were engaged -- there was defence. I don't know that there were any movements. I don't know what kind of operations were going on. I could not conclude based on the conversation that there were any operations going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Well, in the conversation, in fact, the person who you claim isn't you but whose name is Momo Garic said: "We are encircled ..." And then said: "We went down to the town all the way to the Miljacka river but they are too strong there, they are encircling us, and the army refuses to move." And then Prstojevic says: "Wait a second, are you fighting there?" And Momo Garic replies: "We are fighting fiercely. We have many casualties." Does this refresh your memory as to a TO operation involving your TO unit on the 21st of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, before the arrival of the professional army TO members never moved beyond the Sarajevo bypass. I don't think that they ever did. If they did do that, those may have been some individuals for their personal reasons. We didn't have any weapons or means or personnel to go down. The only time that we descended beyond the Sarajevo bypass was in mid-May when the professional army arrived, never before that, save for possibly some individuals. When it came to the organised TO which only defended its lines from paramilitaries, they didn't do that. Only when the professional army arrived - as far as I can remember that was in mid-May - in order to repair the tactical position because the position at Vraca was really not enviable and that's -- we descended down to Grbavica. And that was a semi-encirclement. The location beyond Vraca, Debelo Brdo is a prominent elevation from which you could see Vraca and from which very often sniper fire was opened and there were a lot of wounded, a lot of casualties, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Well this conversation was actually played to Mr. Prstojevic when he gave evidence here, the -- Mr. Karadzic played this intercept for Mr. Prstojevic and Mr. Prstojevic said - and this is at transcript page 13689 and 90: "As for Mr. Garic and his men, I spoke to them several times during that day. He was the commander of the Territorial Defence there. I did not really know the man very well until then and I'm giving him advice here because I see that the JNA doesn't want to do anything. They didn't take part in anything on the 22nd of April either. They didn't help us at all, us in Ilidza. They were rather reserved. Also here they hardly did anything." Now, Mr. Prstojevic, his evidence makes clear that he remembered this as a TO operation and, in fact, that you were the TO commander, and that appears to be consistent with what's in this conversation. Can you explain how it is -- do you have any explanation for your claim that you never spoke to Mr. Prstojevic, you weren't the TO commander, and you have no recollection of this operation?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what else I could tell you other than what I have already said. I know Nedjeljko Prstojevic superficially. Again, I know that he lived and worked in Ilidza, but I do not recall having had a conversation with him, and I'm not aware of there having been an operation outside the Sarajevo bypass, that didn't it include the Sarajevo bypass, and I do want to help here, but there was no hierarchy, there were no appointments that were made until the units arrived. We're dealing with reserve officers, prominent individuals, locals, who established defence lines to defend Serbian homes and this did not move. There was no movement of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Just on that point of geography if we could have P5955 on the screen. This is the map that you marked with your line of defence that we discussed earlier and I'd just like to get you to mark some of the locations that are discussed in this intercept where Momir Garic reports where his men are fighting, which are -- he says: "Vrbanja, Grbavica, Ivan Krndelj and all the way down to Elektroprivreda." So if we could zoom in a bit more. And if we could move down a little bit -- no, the other way, sorry. Up a little bit. Right around if we could put the -- where it says Vraca and the -- that's perfect. Now, Mr. Garic, I'm going to ask you to mark some of the locations referred to in this intercept and the first one is the Vrbanja bridge. Could you put a V where the Vrbanja bridge is, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I can't see this very clearly --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Perhaps we could zoom in on Grbavica a little -- one more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Garic, could you wait a minute until assisted by our usher. We'll zoom in a bit further on Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So that we can still see the red line and the area of Grbavica and the area of the Miljacka river. That would be -- that's perfect.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Are you able to see better now, Mr. Garic, where the Vrbanja bridge is?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now. This is where the river flows --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If we could come --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is kindly asked to speak into the microphone as the interpreter can't hear him.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry, I would like to zoom out again because now we're losing locations on the map I need to have the witness mark. Sorry, before the witness marks the map, I would like to zoom out again. Thanks. That looks perfect.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Mr. Garic, can you see the Vrbanja bridge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Just a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if you could mark it with a V.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if you could mark Ivan Krndelj Street, which probably has a different name on this map than it had at the time, but if you could recognise that street. If you can't find it, that's fine. How about Elektroprivreda, can you see where that location was at the time on this map; and if you can see it, if you could mark it with an E.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Elektroprivreda, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if you could put a circle around the neighbourhood of Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: The Grbavica neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Well, this is Grbavica. The line goes down Zagrebacka Street, Sana Mrkica [phoen], Zagrebacka. This would be the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. And if you could just sign and date that in the bottom right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if that could be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P5956, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I know you've said you don't recall an operation, a TO operation, in this area. But it's -- and you noted that it was clearly beyond the line of defence that you had marked. So if there was an operation in this area on the 21st of April, I take it that would have been an offensive operation by the TO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I am repeating that there was no operation of any kind, no offensive was launched. There was no operation either. The Territorial Defence members didn't go beyond the Sarajevo bypass. I mentioned places, Vrbanja, Grbavica. This wasn't done until the professional army arrived. Perhaps certain individuals went there, but the Territorial Defence never did. I'm speaking about the 22nd of April. It didn't move anywhere. It didn't have any equipment. It didn't have the men. It didn't have the knowledge. It didn't have the weapons. It had nothing. It's when professional military units arrived sometime around the middle of May that they went to Grbavica for the reasons I have already mentioned. In order to prove tactical positions -- well, it's not much of a tactical position, and in order to protect the inhabitants whose ethnicity was still mixed. In Grbavica there were Croats, Muslims, and Serbs. It was in order to protect the inhabitants who were living in Grbavica at the time. And there were paramilitary Muslim individuals and extremists who entered the area and looted the property that belonged to the people who lived there and were the cause of problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Garic, again I'd like to -- our time is limited, if you could please try to focus your answers as much as possible on my specific questions. I'd like to look at another conversation, but I'll just -- -- the transcript of this one which is P5705. This is a transcript of another conversation on the same day, the 21st of April, 1992, between Prstojevic and an unknown male. And we can see at the outset Prstojevic calls and asks: "Is Garic there?" And that's about three lines down. And is told: "Garic went to Pale." "All right. Who am I talking to?" "I am one of his associates," is the response. And Prstojevic responds: "All right. This is Prstojevic speaking, commander of Crisis Staff Ilidza. "Is that so? "Yes." And then the unknown male says: "So, Prstojevic, what's up over there?" And Prstojevic says: "Well, it's good. I sent them the manpower over there." And the male says: "We didn't ... oh, that's from Kasindol; right? "Yes. "Yes, yes, we got there that." And Prstojevic says: "... where are they, tell me? " And the male says: "But they are kind of scattered around. This guy told me that for the part that he received that some of them stayed and that there's about ten of his own men and the rest of them returned." And Prstojevic asks: "Tell me, are the fights still going on down there?" And the response is: "Well, yes. But that's not very organised. The police doesn't want to come out and do their job. One part of the territory is already taken, but the police doesn't want to come out so the people ... I don't know what to tell you. We have problems there." And Prstojevic says: "Tell me, how far will they go. Did you come to the left bank of the Miljacka river?" And the response is: "Yes, this part is taken almost to the Miljacka river. But the upper part, Ivan Krndelj Street, that's still not taken." And Prstojevic asks: "Did you cut through Vrbanja?" And the answer is: "Yes." And Prstojevic says: "And are you in control there?" And the response is: "Well, we are for the moment but the police still didn't come out, so the civilians are holding that, fuck." And Prstojevic says: "Territorial Defence members?" He asks. "And the response is: "Well, yes." And Prstojevic says: "All right, but the police should come out." And the unknown male responds: "Of course it should, but it's not, that's the problem. So Krajisnik called him and he went up there so they can agree on them doing their job and if they don't want ... fuck it, they are not going anything for the last 20 days." And the conversation continues. Now, they're clearly talking about the same operation in the same area we just saw because they mention the Miljacka, Ivan Krndelj Street, and Vrbanja; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Yes, they mentioned them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And it's confirmed in this conversation that it is Territorial Defence members who are engaged. I know you said earlier that you didn't think there was Territorial Defence operation in this area at this time, but does this -- seeing this transcript refresh your memory about that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: This transcript doesn't help me at all. I am repeating once again with full responsibility that the Territorial Defence up until the time when the regular army arrived was not moved. Perhaps certain individuals moved, who knows for what reason. There were individuals who moved, went down, but as for the lines, as for where the Territorial Defence was located, they didn't have the men. They didn't have the equipment. They didn't have enough men to go there. There were no actions, no operations. The status quo was preserved, that's all. All they did was wait until the units arrived. So I've repeated what I've already said, but I don't know what else to tell you, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Also in this intercept we've seen the intercept of, Prstojevic first asked to Garic and he was told Garic went to Pale. And then later in the conversation the same person explains that the police don't want to come out - so it's the Territorial Defence holding the positions - and he says: "So Krajisnik called him and he went up there so they can agree on them doing their job." Do you recall around this time going to Pale to speak with Mr. Krajisnik to get some assistance for your unit?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: As I have said, I often went to Pale in order to deal with certain issues that concern my livelihood. My family and my two children who were 2 or 3 years old and my parents had to be taken to Pale. I had to find accommodation for them there. So I often went to plead, I often went to Pale, and as for Mr. Krajisnik I think -- well, I don't think, I was in his office on one occasion. I spoke to him over the phone on one occasion. And the subject of our discussion concerned my living conditions, or rather, living conditions for my family, my wife, my two sons, and my parents at the time. That is the only occasion on which I was in Mr. Krajisnik's office and I believe that I spoke to him over the phone on one occasion, but the conversation concerned my family problems and solving them so that my family could live in an independent manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to look at another intercepted conversation again from the 21st of April, 1992, and this is 65 ter 30705. And we'll play the intercept, Mr. Garic, and then I'll ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Unidentified female: Good afternoon. "Unidentified male: Good afternoon. "Unidentified female: Could I speak with Mr. Garic? "Unidentified male: And who is this? "Unidentified female: Mr. Krajisnik's cabinet. "Unidentified male: Hold on, please. Hold on. "Momo Garic: Hello? "Unidentified female: Yes. "Momo Garic: Good afternoon. "Unidentified female: Good afternoon. "Momo Garic: Garic, Novo Sarajevo. "Unidentified female: Hold on, please. "Momcilo Krajisnik: Hello? "Momo Garic: Hello? "Momcilo Krajisnik: Is this Momo? "Momo Garic: Yes, it is. "How are you? "Momcilo Krajisnik: Tell me. "I'm all right. Are you all right? "Momo Garic: Well, I'm okay. "Well, there's some problems. Could you receive me up there for a brief meeting? "Momcilo Krajisnik: Well, sure, no problem. "Momo Garic: You could, right? "Momcilo Krajisnik: Sure. "Momo Garic: All right, I'll come them. I'll find some vehicle and I'll come them. "Momcilo Krajisnik: All right, Momo. What's the situation like up there? "Momo Garic: Well, it's all right for the time being. We've had some casualties and many wounded. "Momcilo Krajisnik: You did? Well, are our men withdrawing from up there? "Momo Garic: No, no, but the co-operation here is not on a high level. I don't know why. They are -- "Momcilo Krajisnik: All right, Momo. Come here. Let's not discuss this over the phone. "Momo Garic: All right. "Momcilo Krajisnik: We'll arrange things here. "Momo Garic: All right. "Momcilo Krajisnik: Deal. "Momo Garic: Bye."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Here the speaker identifies himself as Garic from Novo Sarajevo and Krajisnik refers to him as Momo. And the two discuss the situation, and Momo Garic says that: "The situation is all right for the time being. We've had some casualties and many wounded." And Krajisnik says: "Well, are our men withdrawing from up there?" And Garic responds: "No, but the co-operation is not on a high level." Now, you said you remembered that you spoke with Mr. Krajisnik over the phone at the time and that you met with him in Pale, although you claim this was about the accommodation for your family. Does listening to this conversation refresh your recollection as to discussing the situation that your TO unit was in at the time with Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Well, I will repeat what I said. I spoke to Mr. Krajisnik only in order to solve my family problems. As for this subject matter, well believe me I do not remember having had such a discussion. The voice isn't similar. It was just because of my family problems, in order to ensure that they could have an independent existence. They had been displaced. They were -- weren't in their house in Pofalici and that was the period during which I went to Pale on a number of occasions. I did what I could. I didn't have a car. I borrowed a car, hitchhiked there, so this concerned my family problems and nothing else. And while we were above the Sarajevo bypass where the Territorial Defence members were located, well naturally there were quite a few wounded there because there was significant provocations carried out by Muslim paramilitary formations from tall buildings in Grbavica and from behind us where Debelo Brdo was located. So there were men who were wounded. As far as I can remember, there were men who were killed too. These were men who exposed themselves to enemy fire. They would move around freely and didn't abide by the instructions they had been issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just make sure I have your position on this clear. Notwithstanding the fact that the speaker here identifies himself as Momo Garic from Novo Sarajevo and notwithstanding the fact that you were a respected member of your TO at the time and this Momo Garic is describing a situation where there are casualties and wounded, it's your position that this isn't you and you never made such a phone call -- or you never had such a phone conversation with Mr. Krajisnik. Is that how I understand your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Yes, you've understood me. I've understood your explanation too. And let me repeat what I have said. I had contact with Mr. Krajisnik only in order to solve family problems. On one occasion this was in his office in Pale and on one occasion I spoke to him over the phone. I didn't speak to him about the issue that is referred to here.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that intercept, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P5957, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Garic, you knew a Rade Milinkovic from Novo Sarajevo and he was, in fact, a MUP commander in Novo Sarajevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I knew Rade Milinkovic. He was a policeman, a MUP commander -- no, as far as I know he was never a MUP commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Well, in your interview with the OTP in 2004 you said you were -- played an intercept purporting to be between you and Rade Milinkovic and you said: "I know Milinkovic, because if that's the same Milinkovic I know him from Novo Sarajevo. Milinkovic was one of the commanders of MUP." So in 2004 you said that Milinkovic was a MUP commander. Is that right? Or is it now your evidence that he was just a member of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I said that, but I don't remember. I don't recall him being a MUP commander. I know he was a member of the Novo Sarajevo police station. I do know that he was a policeman. As for him being a MUP commander, well, no, I don't recall that. I know that he was a professional policeman and he worked in the Novo Sarajevo police station. The headquarters was behind the Novo Sarajevo municipality at Malta, but I don't recall him having been a commander of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to play another intercept again from the 21st of April, 1992, and this is 65 ter 32780. And again, if you could listen to that conversation and I'll ask you a few questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The French interpreters booth kindly asks to be provided with a transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I understand that transcripts were provided to the booths -- all the booths.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Rade Milinkovic: Hello? "Unidentified female: Is that the local community? "Rade Milinkovic: Yes. "Unidentified female: Garic would like to talk to you. Just a moment ... Momo. "Momo Garic: Yes. "Rade Milinkovic: Tell me, Momo. "Momo Garic: Rade! "Yes. "Momo Garic: Tell me, can we get started? Some of our special guys for fuck's sake? "Rade Milinkovic: We called them. "Momo Garic: And what did they say? "Rade Milinkovic: Nothing call them 611. "Momo Garic: Did Milinkovic call them? "Rade Milinkovic: Who? "Momo Garic: Milinkovic. "Rade Milinkovic: It's me. "Momo Garic: Oh, it's you. "Rade Milinkovic: It's me. "Momo Garic: So what did they say? "Rade Milinkovic: Call 611-338. "Momo Garic: What did I do if you did not succeed? "Rade Milinkovic: Call them. You are the TO commander. "Momo Garic: Oh, my goodness, my goodness. Do you have more cars. "Rade Milinkovic: No. They all check if there are any. "Momo Garic: Sorry. "Rade Milinkovic: They will know if there are any. They already sent to the terrain what they had. "Momo Garic: Yes, but are there any more? "Rade Milinkovic: Well, ask them. "Momo Garic: Anyway. "Is Krstovic up there? "Rade Milinkovic: Yes, he is. "Momo Garic: Send him to see me. "Rade Milinkovic: Fine. "Momo Garic: He organised all of this. "Rade Milinkovic: Okay."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Again, Mr. Garic, we see this is the 21st of April and Momo Garic is again looking for assistance, this time from Rade Milinkovic who you have testified was a MUP officer in Novo Sarajevo, so again this is dealing with your area. And you are identified here as -- or Momo Garic is identified here by first and last name. So again my question is: This is you, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I'm saying that I don't remember. My name is Momir. As far as I could see, this would be either the third or the fourth suspicious conversation in my view. That person should have spent the entire day on the telephone. In one conversation it's about Pale, the second one calling Krajisnik, and that's all on the 21st of April. It doesn't really make much sense. All of that was happening on the 21st April. An unknown person is saying somebody went to Pale, then he speaks to Krajisnik. I really don't -- clear about that -- I'm not clear about that. I can't remember. I told you who I spoke to, and I claim with full responsibility that I don't remember these particular conversations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What I can't understand, Mr. Garic, is that your statement that your name was Momir. Were you not called amongst your friends by the nickname Momo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Moka or Moca, Mocilo, that's what people called me, not Momo.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Mr. Garic, were you aware that the Defence actually listed you as a witness on their witness list under the name Momo Garic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Repeat the question. I did not hear you properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: We received a list of witnesses from the Defence, and you're listed on that witness list as Momo Garic, and that's number 143 of the Defence 65 ter filing. Were you aware that the Defence referred to you as Momo Garic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I did not know the Defence was referring to me as Momo Garic. I signed my statement and everything else as Momir Garic. I didn't know that they listed me as Momo Garic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this intercept as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P5958, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And just to go back to your earlier answer in relation to this conversation, you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have more intercepts to cover?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: One or two, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would like the copies of the intercepts to be delivered to the French booth. I hope the Registrar could make sure. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I understand that sufficient copies were provided and they have to just be distributed among the booths, but maybe the interpreters can confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that, but I wanted to make sure that happens.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: During -- in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Mr. Garic, just in response -- in relation to your earlier answer when I put to you that this was you in the conversation, you said this is the third or fourth suspicious conversation. That person should have spend the entire day on the telephone, and you said it doesn't really make much sense. Is it your position that one or more of these intercepts was fabricated in order to frame you in some kind of way?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I don't know why should anybody frame me. I am a good man and why would anybody fabricate anything against me? But this is suspicious if that person went to Krajisnik and that was not a line from Lukavica-Trebevic-Pale. You had to take a macadam road across villages, across Tvrndic [phoen]. It would have taken at least four or five hours to go to Pale and come back to Pale. And this conversation on the 21st of -- and we've heard already three or four such conversations recorded on the 21st. My personal opinion is that -- I'm not a sinful man. Why would anybody frame me? I have not done anything wrong. Why would anyone frame me? I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. So let's look at another intercept from that day and it's 65 ter 32778 and perhaps before it's played the booths could confirm that they have the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So again, Mr. Garic, this is another intercept from the 21st of April, 1992, and I'd just like you to listen to it and then I'll ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Ranko: Hello? "Ranka: Yes. "Ranko: Ranka, is that you? "Ranka: It's you. "Ranko: Let me talk to Momo Garic. "Ranka: Here. "Ranko: Now, urgently. "Momo Garic: Yes? "Ranko: Oh, Momo, it's you? "Momo Garic: Yes. "Ranko: Ranko speaking. "Momo Garic: Tell me. "Ranko: Who issued the order for us to retreat now? "Momo Garic: Who did? Nobody did. And where from. Where from to -- "Ranko: Fucking hell. "Momo Garic: Where are you calling from? "Ranko: We are stationed. Momo! "Pay attention here. "Momo Garic: Yes. "Ranko: Rave Jankovica Street number 117. "Momo Garic: Yes. "Ranko: That's a building across the street from Palma. There are people in Palma here. We took three to four buildings. "Momo Garic: Are you with Dragisa? "Ranko: We are all alive and well? "Momo Garic: Yes. Is Dragisa there? "Ranko: No, he is not. Dragisa is in 'Palma.' "Momo Garic: Yes. "Ranko: We have everything, the view of the entire surrounding. "Momo Garic: Yes. "Ranko: Send us some people or reinforcement or do something for God's sake. "Momo Garic: We are bringing them in. People from all over are demanding reinforcement. We don't have enough people now for God's sake. "Ranko: Well, send me the army for God's sake. "Momo Garic: All right. "Ranko: Fucking hell ... all right, we'll stay in touch. "Momo Garic: All right. Listen. "Ranko: Yes. "Momo Garic: Is Dragisa there? "Ranko: No, Dragisa is down there, in 'Palma' building. "Momo Garic: But are you in contact with him? "Ranko: Nobody is in contact with anybody anywhere, man. "Momo Garic: All right."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Garic, here is person called Ranko calls and asks to speak to Momo Garic and he is put through, and they proceed to have a conversation. Ranko says that he's stationed at Rave Jankovica Street, across the street from Palma. Now, Palma is a bakery in Grbavica near the stadium and Rade Jankovica Street is a street in Grbavica near Palma; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Palma is not a bakery. Palma is a pastry shop, but indeed it is close to Rade Jankovica Street if that's the Palma we're talking about. I don't know if there is any other. I lived in Sarajevo. It is a pastry shop not a bakery.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. And here Ranko informs Momo Garic that he's stationed there, and he says: "Send us some people, reinforcement, or do something for God's sake." And Momo Garic responds: "We are bringing them in. People from all over are demanding reinforcements. We don't have enough people now for God's sake." And we've seen conversations between Momo Garic and Mr. Krajisnik about reinforcements and between Momo Garic and Prstojevic about reinforcements and Momo Garic and Velibor in Ilidza about reinforcements. So again, I'll put it to you, Mr. Garic, that this is your area, your operation, and this is you speaking, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: This was my sector where the Territorial Defence was up to the bypass and I repeat again, save for a few individuals -- I don't know who this Ranko is let alone that I should have spoken to him. And again, it's the same date, the 21st of April. I really do not understand. Despite everything, I don't understand. I'm not clear on what this is. I claim before this auditorium that Territorial Defence, that its members did not go down beyond the Sarajevo bypass before mid-May. There may have been some individuals who did that for God knows what reasons. But the territorials as a group preserved the status quo. They held their positions in front of their homes, in front of their settlements. They took possession of the Serbian land and they didn't move before the arrival of the professional army.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this intercept as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P5959, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Garic, I'm going to move to another topic now which --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Perhaps that's a good time for a break, Your Honours, if it suits the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. How much longer do you need, Ms. Gustafson?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I think about probably the next -- the entire next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll break for 45 minutes and resume at quarter past 1.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.28 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And just before we begin, I know I mentioned I would probably need the whole session. I think, having looked at the material I'd like to cover again over the break, I think it's more like an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Garic, I'd like to switch topics and discuss the period of time after your TO unit was subsumed within the -- first within the 216th Brigade of the JNA, which then became the 1st Romanija Brigade of the SRK. And you said earlier today that you didn't have an appointment in the JNA, but you weren't a foot soldier either. You said: "I moved around. I moved around the sector. I would go to the command of the brigade but, I repeat, they gave me a lot more free time." So I understand from your answer that you had -- you were at the brigade command at times, so I assume you had some contact with the commander of the brigade, Dragomir Milosevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes. In that territory that we have discussed there was Mr. Dragomir Milosevic's brigade there and I did have contacts with him but not that often.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to play another intercept this time from the 20th of May, 1992, and this is 65 ter 32781, and if you can listen to that intercept and I'll ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Good afternoon. "Is Garic somewhere around? "Who's calling? "Milosevic. "Yes. "So how is it going? Are you doing your job? "This one came from Lukavica and they departed. They will be here soon. And that one, Deva, who left with you said that he saw them up there lining up. "Fine. I saw that up there. "Yes. "There, where Delevoj and I went to ... "Yes. "And there is nothing at Lakic's. "They are on their way. The colleague who was informing there has just the arrived. They are on their way. They should be here any minute. "Fine. "It is postponed a bit. We had a very short time in it. "We have a meeting at 1800. "Until then everything should be done to sort out things completely. "Good. "Please engage our guys a bit more and find out, call, search, and so on. "We have to put the things where they belong to a hundred per cent. "Bye. "Yes, we will. "Bye."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Mr. Garic, is this an example of the contact you had with Dragomir Milosevic at the time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: When I did have contacts, I would pop over to the brigade command. It would happen [as interpreted] often, but I did pop over there. I would see Mr. Milosevic. That was his zone of responsibility. I absolutely -- this does not resemble my voice at all. I did have contacts. I would pop over to the command brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes that there is a mistake in the transcript. The witness said: It would not happen often. I didn't go there often.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So again, notwithstanding the fact that you had contacts with Dragomir Milosevic at the time, you don't believe that this is you speaking in this intercept; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: This does not resemble my voice at all. Believe me. I don't remember. I don't remember this conversation, but I did sometimes go to the brigade command. I had contacts with him and the other officers in the brigade command who were there but not often.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. So when Dragomir Milosevic says in this conversation: "Okay. We have a meeting at 1800 hours." And Momo Garic responds: "Yes." That is consistent with the type of contact you had, what you referred to as popping over to the brigade command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: This does not resemble my voice. I did not have telephone contacts. I would pop over to the brigade command, and there I would see Mr. Milosevic and the officers who were members of that unit's command.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P5960, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And now I'd like to play you another intercept from a few days before this. This is the 12th of May, 1992, and this is 65 ter 32783. If you could again listen to this and I'll ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Unidentified male: Yes. "Radmila Knezevic: Is that the Crisis Staff? "Unidentified male: Pardon? "Radmila Knezevic: Is that the Crisis Staff? "Unidentified male: Yes, it is. "Radmila Knezevic: This is the Serbian MUP. Radmila speaking ... is Momo Garic there? "Unidentified male: Just a moment. "Momo Garic: Yes? "Radmila Knezevic: Listen, we have information that Colonel Milosevic is there with you. "Momo Garic: Yes, he is with me. "Radmila Knezevic: Can I speak to him, please. "Momo Garic: Yes, just a moment. "Dragomir Milosevic: Yes, Milosevic is here. "Momo Garic: Just a moment. "Dragomir Milosevic: Yes ... Milosevic speaking. "Radmila Knezevic: Good morning, this is Radmila Knezevic from the Serbian MUP, a short while ago you were here. "Dragomir Milosevic: Yes, yes, I was. I need you to send someone senior to the staff. "Radmila Knezevic: This is precisely the information I wanted to give you. You have probably left in order to attend an urgent meeting, but in two minutes I managed to find the names of the people. "Dragomir Milosevic: I know. "Radmila Knezevic: They are making the rounds. It will last half an hour and then they will be back there. Where are you going to be when they get back. "Dragomir Milosevic: Look, let someone get in touch with them. They are on the move and then they should come back. "Well, I will wait. Is there anybody -- "Radmila Knezevic: Look, I found a man not from the high leadership but he can come if it's a real emergency. "Dragomir Milosevic: Okay, send him immediately and you can keep calling him via -- "Radmila Knezevic: Don't worry. "Dragomir Milosevic: Very well. "Radmila Knezevic: Have a nice day. "Dragomir Milosevic: Bye."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Garic, here we have Radmila Knezevic calling from the Serbian MUP asking if it's the Crisis Staff, and she says: "Is that Mr. Momo Garic?" And Momo Garic says: "Yes." And she says: "Listen, we have information that Colonel Milosevic is there with you." And Momo Garic says: "Yes, he is." Now, is this an example of your contact with Dragomir Milosevic at the time? Do you recall being at the Crisis Staff with him around the 12th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the headquarters of the Crisis Staff was in Novo Sarajevo municipality. At that time, on the 12th of May, the headquarters was no longer in Novo Sarajevo because we were not in that territory. We were in the territory of Vraca. And I suppose at that time the Crisis Staff had some meetings, perhaps in Lukavica local community or Vraca or something of the sort, but certainly not in the territory of Novo Sarajevo. The headquarters was indeed there until the breakout of the civil war. Again, the voice does not resemble mine. I repeat that I had contacts with him not often and when I did I would go to the headquarters of his brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Vraca was in Novo Sarajevo; right, Mr. Garic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And in this conversation nobody says anything about where the Crisis Staff headquarters are. It's just confirmed that it is the Crisis Staff. So I'm not sure I understand your answer about where the headquarters of the Crisis Staff were at the time. How is that relevant to this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: As far as I'm personally concerned, this doesn't have anything to do with the conversation because I don't think that I spoke to him of the fall. But I told you that the headquarters were in Novo Sarajevo until the war, and when the war broke out the people who were members of the Crisis Staff they crossed over to the Serbian side and to the Serbian territory, and that is the side of Vraca in the direction of Gornji Kovacevici, Miljevici, Lukavica, and Tilava. That's where those people stayed. There were meetings, I suppose some took place in local communes as well. Not all of them took place at the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. So just to confirm your position, do you or do you not recall being with Dragomir Milosevic at the Crisis Staff sometime around the 12th of May, 1992, wherever that Crisis Staff was headquartered at the time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I don't remember Mr. Milosevic appearing at the headquarters, or rather, this outpost of the Crisis Staff. As far as I know, he was in the command and in the field. As for him appearing in the temporary Crisis Staff, where the Crisis Staff would be convened, well, in this case I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to tender this intercept as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, this will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P5961, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And I'd like to now play another intercept from three days after this one, this is the 15th of May, 1992, and it's 65 ter 32779. And if -- once again, if you could just listen and then I'll ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Unidentified male 1: Hello. "Unidentified male 2: Is this the Pajaco headquarters? "Unidentified male 1: Yes. "Unidentified male 2: Is Momo Garic there? "Unidentified male 1: Not at the moment. "Unidentified male 2: Colonel Gagovic wants to speak to him. "Unidentified male 1: Colonel, comrade, how about his deputy? "Unidentified male 2: Okay, here he is. The Colonel is here. Hold on a second. "Budo: Good afternoon. "Milosav Gagovic: Gagovic. "Budo: How are you? "Milosav Gagovic: Fine, thanks, and you? "Budo: So, so. "Milosav Gagovic: Is Momo there? "Budo: Momo went to find Milosevic, tour these positions a little and so we had some ... "Milosav Gagovic: Listen, let him give the three 120-millimetre mortars which you are not using now to the guy who is coming back up to him. "Budo: Just one thing. "Milosav Gagovic: Sorry? "Budo: When is the guy coming? "Milosav Gagovic: He's about to arrive up there. "Budo: Now? "Milosav Gagovic: Right. "Budo: But, okay, let him come and we will send someone too. "Milosav Gagovic: Where are they? "Budo: Down at the base. Our logistics guy he should -- "Milosav Gagovic: Well, you see to it. "Budo: Let him come here. He has a car. He has everything. "Milosav Gagovic: Okay. He'll get everything. "Budo: So we will send somebody with him. I'll write it down and so on. "Milosav Gagovic: Okay. Just call when he gets there. "Budo: Good luck, Colonel. "Milosav Gagovic: I wish you a long life. Good-bye!"

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Garic, here Colonel Gagovic calls the Pajaco headquarters, and you mentioned earlier that at least in April Pajaco was a place where the Serb TO would assemble to discuss matters and that was at transcript page 37. Colonel Gagovic was at the time the assistant commander for logistics of the JNA 4th Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was a colonel or a lieutenant-colonel at the time. I don't know which position he occupied, but I and my comrades, my colleagues, who we contacted in the JNA for help with protecting the Serbian population did go there to ask for weapons to defend ourselves from provocations, attacks launched by the Green Berets at the time that were established in 1991 and to defend against attacks from other paramilitary formations. I knew him personally. I went to the barracks personally quite frequently. That's what I can say.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember him giving you three 120-millimetre mortars that he refers to in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: As far as mortars are concerned, these aren't infantry weapons and, no, we didn't have such mortars, we didn't receive them from anyone. What we had consisted of private weapons that were owned by these locals, hunting rifles, and so on and so forth. As for the weapons issued or distributed by the army, it was a minimum and people retained such weapons as trophies of sorts.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you explain then why Colonel Gagovic is calling the Pajaco headquarters asking to speak with you, being told: "How about his deputy," speaking to a person named Budo, and telling Budo: "Listen, let him," referring to you, "give the three 120-millimetre mortars which you are not using now to the guy who is coming back up to him." Can you reconcile that statement with your claim that you didn't receive any mortars?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I don't remember having received any mortars. Let me repeat what I said. All we had were weapons that had remained behind classical infantry weapons, typical infantry weapons, that had been retained as trophies of sorts.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. And when Colonel Gagovic asks for you, he says: "Is Momo Garic there?" And is told: "Not at the moment," and then -- sorry, the person calling on behalf of Colonel Gagovic says: "Colonel Gagovic wants to speak to him." And then the response is: "Colonel, comrade, how about his deputy?" Now, that appears at least to me to be implicit reference to your role as commander and the role of the person identified as Budo as your deputy. Can you reconcile that comment with your testimony that you had no command position at the time?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Well, I knew Colonel Gagovic who was on duty in Lukavica at the barracks, the Slavisa Vajner Cica barracks, and let me repeat: There were no appointments in the Territorial Defence. This was in mid-May at the time the VRS had been established. As for this reference to Momo Garic, well they were probably used to the fact that I was in the territory with these members of the Territorial Defence and it's probably because he knew me and knew that I would come and ask for weapons on behalf of the people in order to defend ourselves because it was a critical period, it was a very difficult period. We were constantly confronted with the problem of whether paramilitary formations from Mojmilo, Novi Grad, and Debelo Brdo would enter our territory and slaughter the Serbian population. So it's probably for that reason. I don't know of any other possible reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that intercept, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P5962, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now I'd like to go to Exhibit P1478. And while that's coming up, Mr. Garic, just one other question. Do you know a person named Neso Garic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Neso Garic -- well, there's someone called Nenad Garic, Nenad Garic. I don't know a Neso. There is a Nenad Garic who lives in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And is he related to you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And could Neso be a nickname for him?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Well, Nenad is his name. Perhaps Neso is his nickname, but it's Nenad Garic. That's his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could we go to page 28 of the English and page 29 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: This document that I'm about to show you, Mr. Garic, is an extract from General Mladic's notebook from this period of time, and in particular it's an entry from the 30th of May, 1992 -- oh, sorry, the B/C/S -- I was referring to the original Cyrillic. I don't know the page number of the B/C/S. Could we go to the original Cyrillic page 29. Oh, we seem to have it here in -- typed. This is better. Thank you. Okay. Here we see notes of General Mladic of a meeting with unit commanders of the SRK and it says "present" and there's a colon and then it lists a number of people starting with Dragomir Milosevic. And if we could move now to the next page in both languages, you can see some additional people listed as being present. And if we could go to the next page, some further people are being listed as being present. This is numbers 9 and 10. And if we could go to the next page --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: Could we zoom in. The letters are too small. I can't see well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. The page that I wanted you to see -- the minutes of the entire meeting, but the page that I'd like you to focus on is the next page and if we could go to the next page and zoom in. And if you could look at number 12 of the people present at this meeting, it says: "Reserve Captain Momir Garic, commander of the Novo Sarajevo Light Brigade (approximately 730 men)." Now, you told us that you were a reserve captain at this time and -- although Mladic here refers to you as a light brigade commander rather than a battalion commander, it is clear from this entry in Mladic's notebook that you were a commander of your unit at the time and, indeed, you were present at a meeting of unit commanders of the SRK on the 30th of May, 1992, with General Mladic. Is that right, Mr. Garic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: First of all, I was a captain at the time in the Territorial Defence, yes, commander of the light Sarajevo brigade. I'm not aware of such a unit ever having existed. There was the Serbian Territorial Defence. I do remember having attended that meeting, however, but as for being the commander of the Novo Sarajevo light brigade, that's the first time I've heard about this. So this concerned the Territorial Defence, in fact, the people who had organised themselves. There were no particular names here that were used. It was the Serbian Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Well, you've given us evidence that, in fact, the Territorial Defence was incorporated long before this time into the JNA, 216th Brigade, which then became the 1st Romanija Brigade. So according to your evidence, there was no more Territorial Defence at this time. So this is, is it not, a reference to you being a commander of a VRS unit in the SRK on the 30th of May, 1992, and indeed that is why you were present at this meeting that you acknowledged being present at?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I deny that because I know that while I worked in Novo Sarajevo municipality I was involved in all the army establishments, the reserve forces, et cetera. When the Ministry of Defence appeared, the VRS establishment never had such a Novo Sarajevo light brigade, so I find this quite strange. The Novo Sarajevo light brigade. In September 1992, in mid-1992, I became aware of the commands of the units, the establishment of the units, through the Ministry of Defence and this -- Novo Sarajevo light brigade never cropped up. So this is something new to me and something strange.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. And then in light of that answer, do you have any explanation as to why you were included in a meeting of unit commanders of the SRK with General Mladic and why General Mladic referred to you as a commander? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I can't. I don't understand this, but I'm claiming with full responsibility that there was never a unit that was known by this name. From the time the VRS was established with its names, codes, and so on and so forth. But I'm really not aware of anything of this kind. It says it had 730 men, that's quite absurd. In the Tilava-Lukavica-Vraca-Gornji Kovacici-Miljevici-Petrovici area, we never had so many men, although there were some men who weren't fit for military service and also some women. But this name given to the brigade and the number of men that is specified here is something I can't accept.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to move on to another topic, which is the VRS operation to take Grbavica which you discuss in your statement at paragraph 16. This is the statement that's been admitted as your evidence. And you said that this VRS action -- the purpose was to move the line on the left bank of the Miljacka river and gain control of Grbavica. And you said that the purpose was to protect the Serbian majority population in the Sarajevo suburb of Grbavica, which is next to Vraca and other Serbian suburbs. And I think you confirmed in your evidence earlier today that Grbavica was an ethnically mixed neighbourhood, where Croats, Serbs, and Muslims lived together; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: That's correct. They lived together. There was Serbs, Croats, and Muslims, all ethnic groups lived together.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And were you involved in this operation?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I was present, but I did not have the duties of a commander. I was there with the people, all those who entered the 1st Romanija Battalion -- well, we discussed this earlier on and I was one of those who entered that unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. And you said in your statement at paragraph 16 that when you established this line you had old trophy infantry weapons and a few automatic rifles. And you said that -- you took Grbavica with very little fighting, even though as you state in paragraph 17 of your statement that the Muslims had more automatic weapons, hand-held rocket-launchers and small-calibre mortars. Now, whatever weapons you used in this mid-May operation to take Grbavica, it is the case at this time that the SRK within the VRS was very well armed, including with heavy-calibre weapons. And that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: The men from the Territorial Defence at that time up to mid-May, well, they rarely received weapons, other weapons, from the army. From the beginning, from when they started organising these guards, they had these weapons and they had these weapons when they took Grbavica, while in fact they didn't really take it, there wasn't much fighting. The army had their professional weapons, rifles, and so on and so forth. But the Territorial Defence members at the time had trophy weapons, personal weapons, hunting rifles, old M48 rifles, and a few automatic rifles. And it is in this way that they entered the VRS. They did not, in fact, have high-calibre weapons or more efficient weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. I understand from your answer that you don't dispute that the professional army at this time had what you called professional weapons. Now, do you dispute that the professional army at this time also had ample heavy-calibre weapons? And I'm talking about mortars and artillery specifically.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: I don't know. In the sectors I was in and in the field around Vraca and other places -- well, I personally saw that they had personal rifles, semi-automatic rifles, automatic rifles, old M48 rifles. So these were personal infantry weapons, infantry rifles. As far as artillery is concerned, I didn't notice any artillery in that sector. I didn't notice any gun emplacements that were ready to go into action, any artillery ready to go into action. I believe the artillery was kept in the depth behind the commands. I think there's the village of Petrovici in the direction of Klek and Trdonici [phoen], I think they were there, but as for the sector of Vraca and Lukavica, I didn't notice any such weapons in that sector and I didn't notice any such weapons being used.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. So now -- just to go back to this operation to take Grbavica, you said that the purpose was to protect the Serbian majority population there, although you've explained that it was an ethnically mixed neighbourhood. Now, the Chamber has heard some evidence that the taking of Grbavica was part of the goal of the leadership to control the entire left bank or at least much -- much of the left bank of the Miljacka river. Did you ever hear any talk like that, that the Serbs should basically control the left side of the Miljacka?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR GARIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the civilian authorities. I never heard any such thing from the civilian authorities at the time, but there were certain rumours and discussions, according to which it was necessary to improve the tactical position to make it easier to hold those lines. The river Miljacka is a sort of natural barrier and those paramilitary formations couldn't just cross Miljacka and enter Grbavica. So in order to hold the lines with greater ease, given that we didn't have sufficient men because it was an extensive area after all, this had to be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to play you another intercept, and this is a long conversation from the 25th of May, 1992. And because of its length I am just going to play to you certain extracts which will in total be quite lengthy - I apologise for that - but I wanted to give you a fair opportunity to listen to as much of this conversation as possible before I ask you questions. So again, if you could just listen to these extracts from this conversation on the 25th of May, 1992, and then I'll ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have the number for that?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, this is 65 ter 32783.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is that not what we heard already?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Neso Garic: Good day. "Unidentified male: Hello. "Neso Garic: Garic speaking. Is my family namesake there anywhere. "Unidentified male: Yes, yes. "Momo Garic: Yes? "Neso Garic: Hello! "Momo Garic: Hello! "Neso Garic: Where are you? "Momo Garic: Well, here I am. "Neso Garic: I called you the day before last, you know. "Momo Garic: Yes, the lines must have crossed. "Neso Garic: Well, they did. It was some kind of indirect connection, damn-it. Doboj isn't operating. I'm in Banja Luka now, you know. "Momo Garic: In Banja Luka. "Neso Garic: Yes. "Momo Garic: Seriously? "Neso Garic: Well I've come along there's this Assembly session here and so they called me, you know. "Momo Garic: Seriously? "Neso Garic: Yes. "Momo Garic: How are you? "Neso Garic: Well, it's okay. Thank god. Well how are things there? "Momo Garic: Well, so so. "Neso Garic: Hairy. "Momo Garic: Well, damn-it. "Neso Garic: Well, what on earth happened, man, in Pofalici what was that? "Momo Garic: What was it? What do I know what it was? "Neso Garic: Well, there's no one there to do the linking up to organise things. "Momo Garic: Huh. "Neso Garic: Nobody linked anything up. Nobody's organising anything. "Momo Garic: Yeah, right, nobody. They've done things badly there. "Neso Garic: Sorry? "Momo Garic: Well, they had everything there it's just been -- it's just that they weren't unified because to one another they were leaving without one another, running away. They weren't reporting in seriously. "Hell yeah, man, what did you think? "Neso Garic: How on earth could that happen? "Momo Garic: Well, how? How? "Neso Garic: Where are the Elezes? "Momo Garic: I don't know, they're here. "Neso Garic: And what are they? Did they manage to escape or what. "Momo Garic: Well, yeah, they did. "Neso Garic: Well is there anyone left? "Momo Garic: Well, they were the last ones to go, man. "Neso Garic: Seriously? "Momo Garic: Obad there, then this, the people from Donji Pofalici they scrammed. Didn't they ask anyone anything. Soja was the first one to run, with his wife. "Neso Garic: Who? "Momo Garic: Soja. "Neso Garic: Oh, he got married, did he? "Momo Garic: Well, they say he did. "Neso Garic: Who to? "Momo Garic: I don't know, I swear to God. "Neso Garic: Well, how could he do it, damn-it? "Momo Garic: I don't know. "Neso Garic: Why didn't you lot kill him? "Momo Garic: I didn't even see him, I swear to God. "Neso Garic: Well, kill him you lot. Damn! Damn-it. Well don't you -- that's the way to deal with such things. Don't you think that's the way to deal with such things? "Momo Garic: Yup. "Neso Garic: Well, he's a deserter an escapee, an Ustasha. "Momo Garic: Yeah. "Neso Garic: I've had a son. "Momo Garic: No kidding? Well, congratulation, Neso. "Neso Garic: Thanks. "Momo Garic: Did everything go well? "Neso Garic: Yes, thank God. "Momo Garic: Oh! "Neso Garic: Listen, today I might -- the guy's up from Romanija will be coming, you know. "Momo Garic: Yeah. "Neso Garic: I might catch a ride with them by chopper and come up with there with them. "Momo Garic: Where up there? "Neso Garic: Well, up there to Pale a bit. Damn-it. I don't know anything. I should go and see about what to do and how to do it. "Momo Garic: What don't you know? "Neso Garic: Well, I have to see where my parents are, how they're doing, what to do. "Momo Garic: Oh, your parents they've put themselves up in a summerhouse up there near Rajko. "Neso Garic: Yeah? "Momo Garic: First they were at Milanko's place and then they found a weekend house, some house up there, opened it up and settled in. "Neso Garic: Really? "Momo Garic: And Nevena, too, with the kids and -- "Neso Garic: Right, right. "Momo Garic: -- aunt and uncle. "Neso Garic: Well, good for them. Where are your folks? "Momo Garic: Well Dragan is up there at Stjenice. "Neso Garic: I know. Where's uncle? "Momo Garic: And mom and dad are somewhere at, in Pale. "Neso Garic: You don't know where they are? "Momo Garic: I don't know exactly. "Neso Garic: How come, man? "Momo Garic: Hmm. "Neso Garic: Why don't you go to Pale? "Momo Garic: Well when, Naso, damn-it. "Neso Garic: Well, how are things there? "Momo Garic: I don't know. "Neso Garic: That part, are you lot holding anything? "Momo Garic: Well this bit it's holding up. "Neso Garic: Well, would it be possible to keep hold of that, of the left part at least. "Momo Garic: Yes, sure, yes, of course. "Neso Garic: It will? "Momo Garic: Yup, of course. "Neso Garic: Well, hold on to it, damn it. Only what needs doing is that we at least hash up what we don't need on the left side. "Momo Garic: Yep, right, that's the thing. "Neso Garic: Will Mladic do anything to ... he will be coming today, I think. I might be coming with him really. "Will he be doing anything to shell those shits around the barracks. "Momo Garic: Yes. "Neso Garic: Well, he has to, damn-it. "Momo Garic: He will, he will, he will. "Neso Garic: God almighty. "Momo Garic: He will. "Neso Garic: Do you have enough combatants? "Momo Garic: Well, yes, there are a lot of them. "Neso Garic: So the whole lot up there, they scrammed? "Momo Garic: Oh, fuck them. "Neso Garic: Herzegovinians, right? "Momo Garic: Come on man, that's it. "Neso Garic: Seriously?"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness says that there's no interpretation, that he's not receiving anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably the tape played till the end and interpreters were interpreting the -- that into English, that's why you heard nothing in the meantime. Did you till the end of the tape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We're not hearing any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. The microphone was off. Mr. Karadzic said:

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This did not go through because somebody paused it because they thought we were waiting for the interpretation. It would be now necessary to continue listening to this discussion.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Perhaps I can clarify. That was actually just the first three minutes and 15 seconds of the intercept and that was the first section that I wanted the witness to listen to. So that's why the tape was stopped. Now I'd like to move to ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we also hear this part about the Mujahedin that took Pofalici. Maybe it wouldn't be bad for the Trial Chamber to know what this is all about. Who is it who occupied Pofalici after all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, ask it when you have your turn in the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I think his point is that we in listening to the English have not heard the entire transcript. We've only -- it was stopped by the Serbian version, but the English version didn't continue till the end of this portion, so it's probably better actually if they continue the English interpretation before she puts her next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I leave it to you, Ms. Gustafson. But are you sure with the 65 ter number of this?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you give it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 32784, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you told us it's at 783.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: My apologies. The -- exactly what I wanted to play to the witness was played, at least in English, and I believe it was all interpreted. That was up to 3 minutes and 15 seconds. I'd now like to move to 5 minutes and 10 seconds and play up to 6 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Momo Garic: Well, in Pofalici. "Neso Garic: Did they at least defend themselves? They did. "Momo Garic: Well, they'd gathered up at Neno's. A shell fell and killed seven or eight of them straight away. "Neso Garic: Who else was killed up there? "Momo Garic: Well, I know that Zoran Ignjatovic was. "Neso Garic: Where were they targeting them from with the shells. "Momo Garic: Huh? From Buca Potok but our guys claim say our lot fired from Zuc people are going crazy man. "There you go. "Neso Garic: Bloody hell. "Momo Garic: Yeah, they slaughtered close family friendly it seems. "Neso Garic: Which one? "Kum Radislava. "Oh my God. "Momo Garic: These guys were all running and he wanted to fire them from his pistol. And he said where are you running to ... "Neso Garic: Seriously? "Momo Garic: Yeah. "Neso Garic: Who told you that, Milorad? "Momo Garic: The guys who stayed there told me. "Neso Garic: Well ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I'm not hearing anything. I don't receive any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Garic, that was the second portion that I wanted you to hear. Now I'd like to go to 6 minutes and 45 seconds and play until 8 minutes and 25 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Neso Garic: They haven't called you, have they? "Momo Garic: Oh, they have. "Neso Garic: Well, are you the commander up there now. "Momo Garic: Yes. "I am so sick of it all there. If there was any way for me to get ... "Neso Garic: Well, where the bloody hell to? "Momo Garic: Oh ... "Neso Garic: Cut the crap. Well is it you lot who are controlling Mojmilo? "Momo Garic: The top up to the top. There's no going down there. "Neso Garic: So why don't you lot go down there. "Momo Garic: Where man? "We tried ... go where? "Neso Garic: Bloody hell! Well, how? "Momo Garic: Well that has to be done by the air force and strong artillery. "Neso Garic: How come when you're above them? "Momo Garic: I know that but deeper down there along the range. "Neso Garic: Well how come, man? "Momo Garic: Well they are stronger ... "Neso Garic: Zoljas ... "Momo Garic: There's everything. "Neso Garic: Weapons for direct targeting. "Momo Garic: We have everything. "Oh, Neso. "Neso Garic: What? "Momo Garic: That was done over two years ago. "Underground all of it. "Neso Garic: I know. Only the air force could do it. "Momo Garic: Right. That's it. That's the thing. What's the situation in Doboj? "Neso Garic: Well we are holding, you know, it's been liberated but it was poorly done man I'm suggesting certain things ... again ... "Momo Garic: Yeah? "Neso Garic: ... to expel those shits. "Momo Garic: Yeah. "Neso Garic: They don't want to agree to any of it, they're hugging the Muslims and Croats. I'm going to run off because of that, man. "Do you understand? "Momo Garic: Well that's the thing. "Neso Garic: These politicians want to remain all nice and polite and have us, the soldiers, be the war criminals. "Momo Garic: Hang on. There'll be no more civilian - do you know that Crisis Staffs are being abolished? "Neso Garic: It's now War Presidencies. "Same shit. "Momo Garic: Yeah, okay. "Neso Garic: But you can't fathom it, man! I'm going to table a proposal at the Assembly today that the president of the War Presidency ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could go now to 9 minutes and 38 seconds and play until 10 minutes and 29 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Neso Garic: What about Ilidza? Is it holding. "What about Hrasnica. "Momo Garic: I don't know, it's been pretty flattened. "Oh, fuck it, Neso. "They're now saying that our people have gone in down there tanks, to clear out our apartments. What do I know? "Neso Garic: Right. "Momo Garic: I still don't know the precise situation is; what happened just now is a new thing. "Neso Garic: Well, let me tell you. "Well we should take that left part and enough damn it. "Momo Garic: I don't know. We can't discuss it over the phone. I'd like to talk to this when I see you. "Mladic said many things. "Neso Garic: Right, I mean politicians don't have a clue. "I was here I was also at the Assembly. "God damn it, man, they're idiots I take the floor and they're yawning interrupting me three times ..."
